requirement: Support the remainder operator "%". It has the same precedence as "*" and "/" and groups left to right with them. a % b is a - b * (a / b) with "/" truncating toward zero, so the result takes the sign of the left operand ("(1-10)%4" is -1). A right operand of 0 gives the error "division by zero", exactly as for "/".
desc: Evaluate an integer arithmetic expression. First remove every space character from s; parse what remains. Grammar: expr = term, then zero or more of ("+" or "-") term; term = factor, then zero or more of ("*", "/" or "%") factor; factor = a number (one or more decimal digits) or "(" expr ")". Operators of equal precedence group left to right; "/" divides and truncates toward zero; "%" is the remainder a - b * (a / b) with that truncating division, so it takes the sign of its left operand. There is no unary minus. Syntax errors take priority: scanning left to right, at the first point where the next character cannot continue a valid expression, return the error "unexpected end" if the input has run out there, or "unexpected character: " followed by that character otherwise (this includes characters left over after a complete expression). Only if the whole input is syntactically valid, evaluate it; if any "/" or "%" has a right operand that evaluates to 0, return the error "division by zero".

decls.ts: type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: string };
